parts.official_mark_scheme_text: $kx-k=-\frac1{2x}$, so $2kx^2-2kx+1=0$. *M1 — OE, for example $kx^2-kx+\frac12=0$ or $x^2-x+\frac1{2k}=0$; equate the line and curve to form a 3-term quadratic with all terms on one side. Alternatively, using $x=\frac{y+k}{k}$ gives $y=-\frac1{2((y+k)/k)}$ and hence $2y^2+2ky+k=0$. Discriminant $(-2k)^2-4(2k)(1)=0$, so $4k^2-8k=0$, or using the quadratic in $y$, $(2k)^2-4(2)(k)=0$. DM1 — use the discriminant correctly with their $a,b,c$, not in the quadratic formula; DM0 if $x$ is still present. May see $k^2-4(k)(\frac12)=0$ or $1-4(\frac1{2k})=0$. $k=2$ only. A1 — if DM0 then $k=2$ earns A0 XP then B0 B0; allow A1 even if dividing by $k$; if $k=0$ is also present but $k=2$ is used, award A1. $4x^2-4x+1=0$, so $(2x-1)^2=0$ and $x=\frac12$. B1. $y=2(\frac12)-2=-1$. B1. Alternative calculus method: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac1{2x^2}$ or $\frac12x^{-2}$. *M1 — differentiate $-\frac1{2x}$; M0 for $2x^{-2}$; no errors. $[y=]\frac1{2x^2}x-\frac1{2x^2}=-\frac1{2x}$, or $\frac1x=\frac1{2x^2}$ and hence $2x^2-x=0$. DM1 — substitute their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ into the equation of the line or set gradient $=k$ to form an equation in $x$. $x=\frac12$ only. A1 — if DM0 then $x=\frac12$ earns A0 XP then B0 B0. $y=2(\frac12)-2=-1$. B1. $k=2$. B1. Total 5.
